title: Quiz — Thursday night, and the train is climbing
learning_goal: Know that until 1871 the mail for India crossed the Alps on the surface, and feel how new the way through is.

narration.script: It is Thursday night, and the train is climbing. Two years before Fogg, how did this train get to the other side of the Alps?
narration.after_script: Over the top: seventy-seven kilometres of railway laid beside the mountain road, and about five hours. In 1867 you crossed these mountains in the open air. In 1872 you slept through them.

variants.clear: It is Thursday night, and the train is climbing. Two years before Fogg, how did this train get to the other side of the Alps?

after_script_variants.clear: Over the top. Seventy-seven kilometres of railway, laid beside the mountain road, and about five hours to cross. In 1867 you crossed these mountains in the open air. In 1872 you slept through them.

overlays.text: Two years before Fogg: how did this train cross the Alps?
Mont Cenis Pass Railway, 1868–71 · 77 km · summit 2,283 m · 1 in 11
overlays.note: R3: the numbers are on screen, so the guide reads only 'seventy-seven kilometres' and 'about five hours'.

interaction.prompt: Two years before Fogg, how did this train get to the other side of the Alps?

options.text: Everyone changed to a coach in summer, and a sledge in winter
options.feedback: True until 1868 — and it is why crossing the Alps was a story people told for the rest of their lives.

options.text: A railway laid along the mountain road over the pass, gripping a third rail in the middle
options.feedback: Seventy-seven kilometres over the top, a summit at 2,283 metres, gradients of one in eleven, about five hours — and the mail for India went over it.

options.text: The carriages were carried through a tunnel on flat wagons
options.feedback: There was no tunnel yet. That is what the next few minutes are about.

transition.out: cut to the Fell train, then the works
transition.music_cue: none; no sting on the opening date

production_notes: SEGMENT 5, first third (45 s of 215; segment fill 75 % — the chapter maximum — and a 385-word ceiling, of which this scene spends 57). The rundown asks for M-240 'in the feedback', which the player cannot do (feedback is text), so M-240 opens the NEXT scene instead, at 0-10 s, under a caption naming the Fell railway: the answer image lands about two seconds after the reveal is spoken, which is as close to the rundown's intent as the engine allows.
